chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who does not know how much he has prayed—one, or two, or three. He said: “He builds upon certainty, and he performs the two sajdahs of sahw, and he recites a brief tashahhud.”

So this does not contradict the first report, because he said, “He builds upon certainty,” and what certainty requires is recommencing the salat (prayer), as we have explained. And the command regarding the two sajdahs of sahw is to be understood as recommendation, not as compensation for the salat (prayer).

key_terms.اسْتِئْنَافُ: recommencing or beginning the salat (prayer) anew
key_terms.الْجَزْمِ: certainty upon which the ruling is based in the case of doubt
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in salat (prayer)
key_terms.لِجُبْرَانِ: for repairing or compensating for a deficiency

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat (prayer) if he does not know whether he prayed one, two, or three rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling for one who becomes uncertain about the number of rakʿahs prayed in salat (prayer), specifically between one, two, or three. The instruction is to act upon certainty, which in this context is explained as restarting the salat (prayer), while the two sajdahs of sahw are understood here as recommended rather than required to repair the prayer.
